scope: KaoPu Engine function-provider dependency declarations and exact result reuse
problem: A Mother/provider can omit a transitive input while the Engine still forms a stable key from the declared subset, causing a cache hit to reuse a result that is wrong for the current world state.
falsifiableHypothesis: For providers that read state only through an auditable access facade, recording or denying undeclared reads will detect the executed-path counterexample before a reusable result is published; changing the hidden input while the declared subset stays fixed will otherwise produce a key collision with different output.

activation.rollbackPoint: Remove the audit wrapper and retain the existing FunctionAssetContract if one bounded provider trial finds false blocking, unmediated channels, or no discriminating value; do not change production cache behavior in this audition.

teacher.name: Bazel sandboxing and hermetic action model
teacher.specificNovelty: Turn an undeclared input access into an execution failure by exposing only declared inputs, rather than treating a declaration or cache-key equality as proof of completeness.
teacher.boundary: Bazel's default sandbox documentation says host files may remain readable by absolute path; stronger hermetic isolation or a mediated provider access facade is required. Dynamic read observation covers only executed paths.
teacher.integrationDecision: LEARN_PRINCIPLE_NOT_DEPENDENCY; do not add Bazel to KaoPu Engine.

evidenceIncrements.boundedQuestion: How can KaoPu Engine discover a Mother/provider dependency omitted from an exact-reuse declaration?
